newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says EU may set terms on Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: Germany says EU may set terms on Boeing merger.

text.p: Germany said on Tuesday that the European Commission might set conditions for the recent U.S. aircraft industry mega-merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.

A report by Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said the creation of a combined U.S. plane maker with turnover of $48 billion increased the pressure on Europe's fragmented aircraft sector to consolidate in order to compete.
The merger has not yet been reported either to Brussels or to Germany's cartel office, but this is expected to take place either in late January or early February, the report said.

If the Commission is responsible, as appears likely, it will probably not block the merger. But, the report added, EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has already indicated that "terms and conditions" could be set.

The report, reviewed by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet on Tuesday, did not elaborate. But it noted that Boeing's turnover exceeded thresholds activating Brussels' competence in competition regulation.

Germany has already urged the partners in the European Airbus consortium -- of which Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) is a member -- to press ahead with plans to restructure the group into a limited liability company.
Airbus, whose sales are outstripped five-to-one by the new Boeing, must also take a quick decision on whether to develop the superjumbo A3XX project, the report said.
